flashcard_questions.q: What is a sub program in a larger program?
flashcard_questions.a: A named block of code that can be run whenever it is needed.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do sub programs make a program shorter?
flashcard_questions.a: A sub program is written once but can be called many times.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a procedure do about returning a value?
flashcard_questions.a: It carries out a task but sends no value back.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a function send back to the code that called it?
flashcard_questions.a: A single value, passed back using return.

flashcard_questions.q: Which keyword sends a value back from a function?
What is a parameter in a sub program definition?
flashcard_questions.a: A variable listed in the definition that receives an incoming value.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an argument when calling a sub program?
flashcard_questions.a: The actual value you supply when the sub program is called.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do parameters make a sub program reusable?
flashcard_questions.a: The same code can work on different values each time it is called.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a local variable in a program?
flashcard_questions.a: A variable created inside a sub program that only exists while it runs.

flashcard_questions.q: Where can a global variable be read or changed?
flashcard_questions.a: Anywhere in the program, including inside sub programs.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are local variables usually the safer choice?
flashcard_questions.a: They cannot be changed by accident from somewhere else in the program.

flashcard_questions.q: What is file handling in a program?
flashcard_questions.a: Saving data to a text file and reading it back so it is not lost.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the readLine() command return each time it is used?
flashcard_questions.a: The next line of the file.

flashcard_questions.q: Which command checks whether the end of a file has been reached?
Why should a file always be closed after use?
flashcard_questions.a: Changes are saved and the file is freed for other programs.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term-to-definition, 4 causal, 3 command-to-behaviour, 2 scope. Parameter and argument fronts say definition versus call so the classic confusion is tested directly. Dropped the procedure/endprocedure keyword card as low value.
